title: Mines
summary: The mine-finding logic puzzle: safe first tap, logic-only fields, best times
description:
**Mines** is the classic logic puzzle of finding hidden mines on a field of squares, without ads, accounts or tracking.

**What it does**

- **Ready when you open it.** A fresh field waits on the first screen. Your first tap is always safe and always opens an area.
- **Three levels and your own.** Easy (9 × 9, 10 mines), Medium (16 × 16, 40 mines), Hard (16 × 30, 99 mines, turned upright on a phone) and custom fields from 5 × 5 to 50 × 50.
- **Logic-only fields** when you want them: every field can be cleared by reasoning alone, so no game ends on a coin toss.
- **Made for one hand.** Tap to open, long-press to flag, or switch the Reveal / Flag toggle so a tap places a flag. On a computer, right-click flags. Tap a number whose flags are all placed to open the rest around it. Question marks are there if you want them.
- **A hint that teaches.** Hint points to a square that is certain from what is open, or tells you plainly when only a guess is left. Fields where you used a hint don't set best times.
- **Best times and win rate** for every level, with your current and best streak.
- **Easy to read.** Numbers with distinct shapes and colours, squares at least 32 pixels wide, a field that scrolls in its own frame with grid numbers along its edges, light and dark designs, and calmer motion when your device asks for it.
- **Keyboard and screen reader.** Arrow keys move, Space opens, F flags. Every square is announced, for example "row 3, column 5, 2 mines around".
- **Try a field again** after a mine, and pick up a field where you left it.
- **In English or Slovak**, following your phone's language.

**What it never does**

- No ads, no pop-ups between games, no paid unlocks.
- No account and no sign-in.
- No internet access at all: the app cannot connect to the internet.
- No analytics or tracking of any kind. Your times and statistics stay on your phone.

research.used_for: The expected controls and rules of the type: tap or left-click to open, long-press or right-click to flag, opening the neighbours of a satisfied number, a first square that is never a mine, the three usual level sizes (9 × 9 with 10, 16 × 16 with 40, 16 × 30 with 99) plus custom sizes, a timer that starts with the first move, and fields solvable without guessing as a mode.
Complaints about phone versions of the type: banner and full-screen ads after each game in the free apps (from a site that promotes its own browser version, so read as anecdotal).
Store reviews: players dislike fields that end in a 50/50 guess and want every field solvable by logic, which led to the logic-only option and to a hint that says when only a guess is left.

Store listing (read from a search result summary; the page itself refused the request): no-guess fields and opening around numbers are selling points, and some apps lock no-guess mode and automatic flagging behind unlocks. Here every feature is free.
An ad-free version of the type; a review notes the missing desktop shortcut of opening around a satisfied number, which confirmed that tap-to-open-around-a-number belongs in the core flows.

Review complaint that a long-press was taken as a short tap and opened a mine: led to the visible Reveal / Flag toggle, an adjustable long-press time, a visible press ring, and ignoring a press that moves.
